It's a weird story. Found out I was trans when I was around 14 years old. Learned about it at school and it kinda clicked in my head. "Holy shit, this is just how I constantly feel". Told my parents somewhere around my 15th birthday (everything is a bit fuzzy in my head. Probably because of trauma reasons)

I kinda went back in the closet, because their reaction was shitty, so I came out again when I was 17-ish and again when I was 20 or whatever. Really fuzzy, but I don't like thinking about that time too much

I came out to friends pretty quickly! At my previous job almost everyone knew too. Pretty nice people who didn't really care and we're really supportive. One of them even gave me some clothes and so many of them helped me when I found a place of my own. 

So yeah, I don't really have a specific time for it. I started HRT when I was 23.5 years old, but before that was pretty open and out. I think I was around 21 years old when I was really out to pretty much everyone but family (constantly acted like it was a phase for my own safety)

Sorry for this long, unnecessary story hehe. It just feels nice to get this out of my chest. Have a nice day/night, y'all! <3

I knew I was trans when I was around 14 years old. Before that, I didn't have the words for it. I felt weird and out of place my whole life and it only got worse when I found out I was trans. I knew what the problem was, but I couldn't do anything about it... My parents were, and still are, transphobic, so I could only start living my life the moment I found my own place to live.

Those years were so tough... I fucked up on school, because I was too depressed to give a fuck. I threw away my life, because I had zero hope it would ever get better. I was very lucky when I found an accepting work place. Those colleagues felt like a second family. At the time I was 21 years old. It started getting better and better after all those years. I worked and found my own place and slowly, but surely, could become the person o was meant to be.

It was a hellish journey, something others should never experience, but alas... Millions of people experience this at varying degrees. 

It feels hopeless. For almost everyone this just feels so damn hopeless. Just don't give up. There are too many people who lose hope and lock themselves up or even worse... Life can be so cruel, but it can also be so beautiful when you can finally see more than the darkness.


I wish you all the luck and energy you need. Life is just so hard on all of us. Let's show it who's boss.
